tldr: Mid-October arXiv papers extended multimodal LLMs with tool use and reasoning-driven embeddings. Late October work turned to when models should refuse and how vision and language modules exchange information.
whats_new: VIGOR, an arXiv preprint, orders token unmasking by visual gain to reduce hallucination in multimodal discrete diffusion language models.
why_it_matters: Multimodal failures, such as answering without enough visual evidence or losing perception under small perturbations, are reliability issues for any pipeline that feeds images to a model.

beats.headline: Visual tool-use and reasoning-aided embeddings
beats.summary: Two papers push MLLMs beyond internal reasoning alone.

beats.headline: When should a multimodal model refuse?
beats.summary: Studies refusal when an image gives insufficient evidence.

beats.headline: Latent communication replaces text between modules
beats.summary: Two papers pass continuous representations instead of discrete text.

beats.headline: MIRA targets the perception-reasoning gap in RLVR
VIGOR mitigates hallucination in diffusion LLMs
beats.summary: Extends hallucination mitigation to non-autoregressive multimodal models.

open_questions: Do any of these preprints release code or results on a production vision-language model?
Does VIGOR's hallucination gain hold on benchmarks beyond the ones in the paper?
take_for_builders: If you ship vision inputs, add an insufficient-evidence refusal case and a perturbed-image case to your evals; these preprints are unreplicated, so verify on your own data.
